title: Observation of complete delocalization in disordered photonic lattices
abstract: We present the exceptional phenomenon of complete absence of Anderson localization, and perfect transmission of particles, in a completely disordered diamond-dot chain. We analytically show a proof for the condition to observe this exceptional phenomenon, based on a transparent window emerging from a geometrical condition. We support our theoretical prediction by numerical simulations and direct experimental observation of the transmission probabilities of the light in a femtosecond laser-written diamond-dot photonic lattices. We additionally show that for a $π$ effective magnetic flux, extreme localization of the light in the same system may occur, independently on the specific geometry. Our results open up an excellent platform for controlling the transmission of energy from ballistic to zero transmission, in a completely disordered lattice system..
summary: The paper demonstrates that perfect energy transmission can be engineered in highly disordered photonic lattices by tuning the lattice geometry to a specific critical condition. Using both theory and experiment on diamond-dot structures, the authors show this mechanism allows for precise control over wave localization, moving from localized states to ballistic transport.
main_problem: The study investigates the phenomenon of complete absence of Anderson localization (AL) and perfect energy transmission in a completely disordered photonic lattice.
main_result: Perfect, ballistic transmission is achieved when the geometry approaches a critical condition ($\Delta = \Delta_c$), allowing for control over energy transport from localized to perfectly transmitted states.
method: The research combines analytical theoretical proofs with numerical simulations and direct experimental measurements using femtosecond laser-written photonic lattices.
model_or_system: The system is a disordered diamond-dot (DD) photonic lattice, modeled by a tight-binding Hamiltonian mapped to an effective 1D model. The disorder is controlled via geometrical parameters like the hopping ratio ($\Delta$) and an applied effective magnetic flux ($\Phi$).
key_observables: Transmission probability ($T$), which is measured experimentally as intensity output profiles (IOI) and theoretically calculated based on energy $E$.
important_parameters: The critical geometrical parameter $\Delta_c = 1/\sqrt{2}$ and the effective magnetic flux $\Phi$ are crucial for controlling transport regimes.
main_assumptions: Initial analysis assumes symmetric geometries ($d_x = d_y$) for simplicity, though the core physics relates to disorder-induced localization/delocalization transitions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the random DD chain structure, show transmission probability dependence on energy and geometry ($\Delta$), and present experimental intensity profiles confirming high transmission near critical geometries.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing the theoretical model (tight-binding Hamiltonian), analytically deriving the condition for perfect transmission ($\Delta = \Delta_c$), supporting this with numerical simulations showing flux effects, and finally validating the findings through direct experimental measurements on fabricated photonic lattices.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete platform—photonic crystals—to study fundamental concepts of wave localization (Anderson localization) in disordered media, offering an optical analogue to solid-state physics problems relevant to quantum transport.
